title: Updates off means off: mistyped values, silent offers, same-version repairs and the version number an old orion loses
summary: updateMode is read once, after the session-start pull, ignoring case and spaces; off (or any value orion does not understand, with a warning every session) now silences the update, rules-check, status-line and mods offers; a new orion.sh repair restores missing orion files at the installed version and replaces the update --force advice in the skills; a project an old orion.sh updated gets its version number back.
lessons_learned: A setting the session-start pull can change must be read after that pull; moving a read earlier in check reopened that gap.

deferred.what: In a git project whose committed VERSION has an empty line 5 (every project an old orion.sh updated), the silent fill leaves .claude/orion/VERSION modified in the main checkout, so the same session start asks to ship orion's uncommitted files, and until that ships a later session-start git pull --ff-only that brings a VERSION change is refused.
deferred.why: Whether the hook may write a tracked file there, or how the uncommitted check treats that fill, is a design choice the issue did not take.

deferred.what: The check 'init with a BOM in settings.json' with the PowerShell editor failed once on unchanged default-branch code and passed on every later run, so it looks flaky and can turn a later gate red by chance.
deferred.why: Outside the issue's seam; the cause was not found.
